topic: Stacked Tiny Sprinkler stall and visible cycle timing
currentUserGoal: Prevent accumulated Tiny Sprinklers from appearing to stop after a while, make their combined cycle shorten as more are owned, and clearly distinguish real resource starvation from a broken cooldown.
workCompleted: Traced the apparent cooldown stack to recipe capacity behavior rather than timer accumulation.
Found that a full Moisture buffer clamped the entire Tiny Sprinkler recipe to zero, silently canceling Care or Growth output, automated touches, healing, pulses, and animation.
Added overflow-safe secondary recipe outputs and marked Tiny Sprinkler Moisture overflow-safe in both Caretaker and Cultivator modes.
Preserved genuine recipe pauses: an empty Dew buffer still stops the sprinkler and a full primary Care or Growth buffer still applies normal capacity behavior.
Added a shared stack-cycle interval calculation so additional sprinklers visibly shorten the combined cycle time.
Changed helper field badges from touches-per-second to the real stack interval, such as 0.27s for six rank-one sprinklers.
Changed input-starvation badge copy to explicit labels such as NO DEW instead of an unexplained PAUSED state.
Extended the redesign DOM snapshot with Tiny Sprinkler cycles, progress, interval, pause reason, and relevant resource buffers.
Added deterministic regression coverage for six rank-one sprinklers running for ten seconds with a saturated Moisture tank.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 221 Vitest tests across 26 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
The regression test confirms six rank-one sprinklers have an approximately 267.094 ms combined cycle and complete 37.44 cycles in ten seconds while Moisture remains full.
Desktop redesign verification at 100x100 with twelve sprinklers showed cycles advancing, a 43.403 ms combined cycle, no pause, 144 FPS, zero frame spikes, and no full-field scans.
Phone-sized 390x844 verification showed cycles continuing, no final pause, 144 FPS, zero frame spikes, no full-field scans, and no browser warnings or errors.
Vercel production deployment dpl_FktCoLuj3wYCDAPN1UdWXdSfU3Be reached READY and was aliased to grasstouchingsimulator.com.
The Mac mini fast-forwarded to 20582ea and completed its own strict TypeScript and Vite production build.
knownIssues: A sprinkler can still correctly pause when Dew is exhausted or its primary output is full; the field badge now exposes Dew starvation explicitly.
Overflow-safe Moisture is intentionally discarded when its tank is full so the sprinkler can continue its primary work.
The browser stress metrics reflect the current desktop display and a responsive phone viewport, not a physically slow phone CPU.
The unrelated docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md remains untracked and is not part of this slice.
nextRecommendedSteps: Hands-on test a long run with several sprinklers and watch for the cycle badge to shorten as copies are purchased.
Confirm NO DEW is understandable when the actual input buffer runs dry.
Apply overflow-safe byproducts to other recipes only when their secondary storage demonstrably cancels a more important primary action.
doNotRevert: Do not make a full Moisture tank cancel Tiny Sprinkler Care, Growth, automated touches, healing, or pulses.
Do not add one independent timer or Phaser event per helper copy; stack throughput remains aggregate model work.
Do not label genuine input starvation as a generic unexplained cooldown.
Do not include docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
